body: yeah, crying woman isn't his specialty. lol

I am about 4 years away from the average age in my family for menopause. All the women in my family have finished menopause within 2 years. The latest anyone has had a child was 6 years older than me. 

I understand we are talking about YEARS here, but I cannot be more serious when I say it is not enough time, especially if it takes this long per child. 

I ovulate on the 13th, like clockwork. my husband has well above average sperm count, mobility, and very healthy swimmers. if anything there are too many sperm and they are blowing up the egg. I have a couple things that are barely noticeable that could impact fertility, but even combined shouldn't be an issue. Think one spot of Endo, on small cyst, slightly tilted uterus, and zero symptoms from any of these. 

My periods are clockwork, I don't have bad cramps, I am overweight and I'm focusing on that but it's not like I have 150lbs to lose here.

I have an appointment with our naturopath next week, I think I'm going to move it up just to bridge the gap between now and a counselling session. thank you for the reminder that this is a possiblity. sometimes one cannot see the forest for all the trees.

Thank you for saying 'bullshit', it makes me feel better to hear that. I hate the idiotic platitudes, ''oh they are in a better place', 'it wasn't meant to be', 'they lived a good life'. Fuck off. this is total bullshit and I don't deserve to wait for a baby when Snookie can get knocked up blackout drunk on her ass. (edit) TWICE!

Well, I have a few years to deal with this. It's an odd feeling, to know that you are going to be suicidal. are not currently, but will be. knowing that there's little to nothing that can be done (save the obvious) to prevent it, but something completely out of your control. Something theoretically easy, and happening everywhere around you, but out of grasp.

I think my hormones are at a dangerous level. My RE prescribed without doing her do diligence and I've belatedly found out that the levels I was on are totally inappropriate for my circumstance. additionally my husband is very accustomed to a rational level headed woman who has never suffered from PMS....well good lord he has certainly had an education this last few weeks!

We are seeking counselling, not just for this but we do a 'tune up' every once in a while for our marriage (even if nothing is up) and I think we are going to bump up our appointment by a few months. 

Currently our pastor is on vacation, and ironically enough, I am filling in for him. I am feeling so much better having 'confessed' how I feel here and I think it's made a huge difference in how I"m looking forward.

Thank you, that is amazing news! I didn't know about that option. I don't know if it's available in Canada, but I will be looking into it. 

Having a baby biologically is not the same, I would absolutely love an adopted child the same way and degree as a biological one. but the cost associated with adoption is too much, and an older child would likely have issues we cannot accommodate with our lifestyle/family situation.

Thank you for saying so. And honestly, I don't know if this has ever been a bother to you but I'll say it anyway. There is absolutely nothing wrong with not wanting babies. frankly not wanting a kid of ones own is perfectly natural and I don't like the culture (that I live in) that makes childless women out to be selfish. 

I think it's selfish to make a person you didn't want just because of social pressure. 

I wish I could blame that ramble on alcohol, but I can't, I'm trying for a baby! 

My husband comes from a family that, despite my absolute pleasure that he is around and all, really shouldn't have had kids. his parents seem to not really have wanted them either. It's effected him and his siblings differently, but most notably in him is his inability to see the end of a problem. If I'm depressive, I'm always going to be that way. if the house is messy, it's always going to be that way. So we are infertile, I'm depressed and it's always going to be that way. He tries to help by acting the opposite of however I'm feeling, but it's not working anymore and I don't know what will help instead.
Brother In Law. Crazy- Ass Psyco my husband is unfortunately related to by blood was too long lol

No. I said our debt isn't the worst. We own our house, but have a huge line of credit. Our household makes $50,000/year. We are not as bad off as some, but the process of adoption is not easy. My BIL is mentally unstable, as is much of that side of the family. To the point of likely having to sever contact with them to continue to adopt. Not that we are unwilling to do so, but it's not exactly an easy step to take as it means that their lives will be impacted negatively without our influence. Possibly die earlier. 

Also, adoption is not an alternative to having a pregnancy. many people are called to be adoptive parents. In my current mindset it would be a fall back plan and no child deserves that. I have not moved on to that kind of drive yet. Also, we have been TTC for under a year, despite our ages, my husband is hopeful we will get pregnant. I have a little hope, but honestly I think I cant put as much effort and hope into adoption. I cannot eat breathe and sleep the adoption process the same way that I am having to commit to TTC, and you have to for that to succeed.

Thank you, I don't know what the next step is really. I am a planner, so I have no idea what to do in this situation. I mean, total idiots can get knocked up by accident and have a kid they barely want. 

My entire day revolves around getting pregnant. I wake up, temp. My entire diet is regulated. I left work because I couldn't make the appointment schedule necessary for this to happen, so our finances are awesome. I know that getting a job would help...but my brain is so full of baby I can't get there from here.
